title: Directed Activities in a Fitness Room
summary:
Pregnant women without medical contraindications should do at least 150 min of moderate-intensity activity per week, following ACOG guidance. Group fitness classes offer a safe, social, and motivating setting, but each one must be adapted to the trimester, the woman's prior fitness, and pregnancy's physiological changes.

The chapter goes through Pilates, yoga, indoor cycling, HIIT, Body Pump, Body Combat, aquafitness, functional training, Hyrox, CrossFit, and choreographed classes. For each it lists key adaptations, an example session, and benefits. Common themes are avoiding impact, prolonged lying on the back, and overheating, keeping effort moderate (RPE 12-14), and having trained professionals guide the class.
points: At least 150 min per week of moderate-intensity activity is recommended for women without contraindications.
Prenatal Pilates is best 2-3 days a week, avoids prolonged supine work from the second trimester, and favors quadruped, seated, or standing positions.
Prenatal yoga avoids inverted postures and deep twists and emphasizes relaxation and visualization in the third trimester.
Indoor cycling uses a cadence of 60-80 rpm, heart rate at 40-60% of maximum (or RPE 12-14), no sprints, and 2 days a week.
HIIT stays at RPE 12-14 with short intervals, long recovery, six to eight rounds of 20-40 s, and no jumping or sudden direction changes.
Group strength classes reduce load to 40-60% of usual weight and avoid the Valsalva maneuver; CrossFit loads are 50-60% of 1RM.
Water reduces body weight by up to 50%; aquafitness is best 2-3 days a week.
Functional training uses light equipment such as bands, a ball, and weights under 5 kg; Hyrox keeps distances and times to 50-60% of standard and replaces running with brisk walking or cycling.
The chapter states group exercise reduces pregnancy complication risk by up to 40%, and that classes also reduce anxiety, depression, and lower back and pelvic pain.
takeaways: Choose low-impact options and avoid jumps, sudden turns, and explosive moves.
Keep effort at RPE 12-14 and stay hydrated in a well-ventilated space.
Reduce weights substantially and breathe out during exertion.
After the first trimester, avoid long periods on your back and use side-lying, seated, or standing positions.
Build sessions with a warm-up, a main block, and a cool-down with stretching and breathing.
Use trained instructors and tailor the class to your level; Hyrox and CrossFit suit very active women or athletes only.
cautions: Avoid overheating during cycling, CrossFit, and other intense classes.
Avoid exercises that raise abdominal pressure or strain the linea alba, such as burpees, crunches, sit-ups, toes-to-bar, and kipping.
Hyrox-style work should be done only by very active women or athletes who know the proper technique.
